themes_detail.label: Maintenance Crisis at City Facilities
themes_detail.summary: Maintenance or facility complaints spiked to 39 THIS WEEK, up 906% from the 3.9 weekly average over the prior 8 weeks (z-score: 11.33), signaling a sudden breakdown in upkeep across parks, playgrounds, or public buildings in Throgs Neck/Co-op City that demands immediate investigation into what facilities are failing.
evidence: 39 maintenance/facility complaints THIS WEEK vs. 3.9 weekly baseline (906% spike, z-score 11.33)
This represents the single highest z-score spike in the dataset, indicating a statistically extreme anomaly
Timing suggests a specific trigger event or systemic failure rather than gradual deterioration
reporting_angles: Which specific parks, schools, or public buildings are generating the surge—site visits to document conditions
Interview Parks Dept, DOE, or NYCHA officials on staffing cuts or deferred maintenance budgets affecting the district

themes_detail.label: Unregulated Mobile Food Vendors Flooding District
themes_detail.summary: Mobile Food Vendor complaints exploded to 4 THIS WEEK, a 3100% spike from the 0.1 weekly average (z-score: 11.72), suggesting either a new vendor operation or enforcement vacuum allowing unlicensed street food sales to proliferate in Throgs Neck/Co-op City.
evidence: 4 mobile food vendor complaints THIS WEEK vs. 0.1 weekly average (3100% increase, z-score 11.72)
Paired with vendor enforcement spike of 1500% last week (4 complaints vs. 0.2 avg), indicating residents and inspectors are both flagging vendor activity
Both spikes suggest a coordinated enforcement action or sudden influx of unlicensed vendors
reporting_angles: DOHMH and DOC enforcement officials: are there known problematic vendors or areas in the district?
Street-level reporting: where are these vendors operating and what complaints are residents making (sanitation, blocking sidewalks, noise)?

themes_detail.label: Tree Health Deterioration Accelerating
themes_detail.summary: Dead/Dying Tree complaints jumped to 10 LAST WEEK, up 567% from the 1.5 weekly average (z-score: 5.38), indicating rapid environmental decline in the district's street tree canopy that warrants investigation into disease, pest pressure, or deferred Parks Dept maintenance.
evidence: 10 dead/dying tree complaints LAST WEEK vs. 1.5 weekly baseline (567% spike, z-score 5.38)
Highest spike for environmental issues in the dataset, suggesting concentrated problem in specific neighborhoods or street blocks
Aligns with 317 building permits filed (mostly alterations) which may include tree removal or site disturbance
reporting_angles: Parks Dept arborist: which tree species are dying and why—pest outbreak, disease, drought, or salt damage from winter?
Map the 10 complaints to identify geographic cluster—are they concentrated on one avenue or throughout the district?

themes_detail.label: Rodent Infestation Surge
themes_detail.summary: Rodent complaints spiked to 4 LAST WEEK, up 433% from the 0.8 weekly average (z-score: 7.51), a statistically severe spike that coincides with increased unsanitary condition and litter complaints, suggesting a public health threat from pest activity and waste management failures.
evidence: 4 rodent complaints LAST WEEK vs. 0.8 weekly average (433% spike, z-score 7.51)

Litter Basket Complaint spike (1500%, 4 complaints 2 weeks ago vs. 0.2 avg) and high baseline unsanitary conditions (227 complaints over 90 days) suggest inadequate waste removal fueling rodent populations
Convergence of three sanitation-adjacent complaint types points to systemic waste/pest management failure
reporting_angles: DOHMH pest control and Sanitation Dept: are they seeing elevated rat activity in Throgs Neck/Co-op City, and is this connected to trash collection or illegal dumping?
Community impact: interview residents in areas with high rodent complaints about health and property damage

themes_detail.label: Noise and Safety Incidents Cluster
themes_detail.summary: Noise complaints surged to 24 TWO WEEKS AGO (167% above the 9.0 weekly average, z-score: 4.16) and Safety complaints hit 6 (500% above 1.0 weekly baseline, z-score: 5.77) during the same period, suggesting either a specific event or emerging hotspot of disruptive and unsafe activity.
evidence: 24 noise complaints TWO WEEKS AGO vs. 9.0 weekly baseline (167% spike, z-score 4.16)
6 safety complaints TWO WEEKS AGO vs. 1.0 weekly baseline (500% spike, z-score 5.77)
Temporal convergence suggests both noise and safety concerns tied to the same incident or location, rather than independent trends
reporting_angles: NYPD crime and incident data: what happened in Throgs Neck/Co-op City 2 weeks ago—were there arrests, gang activity, or a major event?
Canvas residents in the highest-complaint neighborhoods about what triggered the noise and safety spike
